research_question: How accurately can ArchSync reconstruct software architecture components and relationships from TypeScript source code?
unit_of_analysis: Expected or predicted component and relationship per D1 repository state; annotated detector signal per D2 source location
metrics: Node and edge precision, recall, F1, and exact changed-graph agreement; detector-signal TP, FP, FN, TN, precision, recall, F1, and specificity
denominator_or_comparator: D1 graph items aggregated over 20 independently applied patches; D2 has 20 positive and 20 hard-negative signals
dataset_or_data_source: D1 Order Platform phase-2 evidence; D2 TypeScript detector challenge evidence
paper_section: Section 4 RQ1; Section 8 Evaluation Methodology; Section 9 Results RQ1

research_question: How accurately can ArchSync distinguish no-impact changes, architecture-rule violations, and architecture evolution?
unit_of_analysis: One independently applied D1 source-code patch and its expected violated-rule identifier set
metrics: Exact three-class agreement; exact violated-rule-set agreement; P3 PASS, BLOCK, or REVIEW decision agreement
denominator_or_comparator: 20 D1 patches: 9 no-impact, 7 violation, and 4 evolution; rule-set denominator is 7 violation cases
dataset_or_data_source: D1 Order Platform phase-2 evidence and P3 Git-diff replay evidence
paper_section: Section 4 RQ2; Section 8 Evaluation Methodology; Section 9 Results RQ2

research_question: How accurately can ArchSync localize architectural findings in source code?
unit_of_analysis: One finding-bearing D1 patch with at least one expected file and exact source line
metrics: Expected-file agreement and exact-line agreement; column, detector, excerpt, and model path retained as diagnostic evidence but not separately scored
dataset_or_data_source: D1 Order Platform phase-2 evidence and P3 Git-diff replay evidence
paper_section: Section 4 RQ3; Section 8 Evaluation Methodology; Section 9 Results RQ3

research_question: Are ArchSync full-repository and Git-diff outputs deterministic and reproducible, and what analysis scope and latency are observed for the cached incremental gate?
unit_of_analysis: Duplicate normalized analyzer execution; one cold and one warm P3 check per patch; one parsed TypeScript file instance; one measured gate run
metrics: Byte-identical normalized replay; cold/warm agreement; incremental/full-scan equivalence; cache-hit agreement; parsed-file fraction; descriptive median and p95 latency
denominator_or_comparator: 42 D1 current-version executions; duplicate D2 runs per pinned version; 20 P3 cold/warm pairs; 189 TypeScript file instances; 20 latency samples per mode on the recorded Windows environment
dataset_or_data_source: D1 and D2 replay evidence; P3 Git-diff evidence and raw timings
paper_section: Section 4 RQ4; Section 8 Evaluation Methodology; Section 9 Results RQ4

research_question: To what extent does AI-assisted development create architecture drift compared with human development?
unit_of_analysis: One independently assigned feature or commit produced under a frozen human or AI-assisted experimental condition
metrics: Architecture-drift violation rate per commit and per feature; drift-type distribution; time to first drift; severity; effect size and uncertainty defined before data collection
denominator_or_comparator: Frozen comparison among human-only, AI without guardrails, AI with architecture context, and AI with ArchSync; denominator is commits and completed features per condition with participant and task balance
dataset_or_data_source: Future multi-condition study logs: repositories, commits, feature outcomes, prompts, model and tool versions, timestamps, and independently adjudicated drift labels
paper_section: Not a current-paper RQ; future protocol and paper; current paper only supplies deterministic measurement prerequisites
evidence_or_next_gate: Freeze participant/task sampling, assignment, drift rubric, model versions, power or precision target, and analysis plan before collecting outcomes

research_question: Does combining architecture specification, source code, infrastructure-as-code, and runtime evidence improve architecture-drift detection?
disposition: Code-only prerequisite in current paper; full question in a future paper
unit_of_analysis: One declared or observed relationship, source-specific evidence item, or finding under a frozen code-only versus multi-source ablation condition
metrics: Precision, recall, F1, false-positive and false-negative counts, unsupported-claim rate, conflict rate, and per-source ablation delta
denominator_or_comparator: Same independently annotated cases evaluated under code-only, code plus IaC, code plus runtime, and all-source conditions; denominators frozen per relation, evidence item, and finding
dataset_or_data_source: Current D1, D2, and P3 code-only baseline plus future P5 IaC and P6 runtime benchmark with source-wise ground truth and ablation outputs
paper_section: Current Sections 4 and 8-10 establish only the code-derived feasibility baseline; full multi-source evaluation belongs to a future paper
evidence_or_next_gate: Current code-only evidence is verified; next gate requires implemented IaC and runtime observers, frozen multi-source ground truth, ablations, raw outputs, and verifier

research_question: To what extent can an LLM explain root causes and generate repairs that preserve the approved architecture?
unit_of_analysis: One deterministic finding, one generated explanation, and one candidate repair evaluated in an isolated sandbox
metrics: Root-cause correctness under a frozen reviewer rubric; evidence-citation coverage; unsupported-claim rate; repair apply rate; conformance pass; regression-test pass; repair success; time to fix
denominator_or_comparator: All selected findings receive the frozen generation and verification procedure; denominators reported for explanations, attempted repairs, applied repairs, and verified repairs
dataset_or_data_source: Future P4 explanation and repair benchmark, prompt and model-version log, generated patches, sandbox test outputs, conformance rechecks, and blinded reviewer labels
paper_section: Not a current-paper RQ; current Sections 4 RQ2-RQ3 provide findings and evidence only; future protocol and paper required
evidence_or_next_gate: Implement the deterministic-before-LLM boundary, freeze the reviewer rubric and sandbox protocol, then retain every prompt, output, patch, test result, and conformance result

research_question: Can continuous architecture governance reduce drift without an unacceptable loss of developer productivity?
unit_of_analysis: One pull request, feature, or review session in a frozen baseline-versus-governance study condition
metrics: Escaped and introduced violation rate; development time; merge delay; false-block burden; approval count and approval load; architect decision time; token, compute, and runtime cost
denominator_or_comparator: Comparable tasks and teams under baseline and ArchSync-assisted conditions; denominators reported per pull request, feature, participant, and study condition
dataset_or_data_source: Future real pull-request pilot with Git and CI event logs, gate decisions, review actions, timestamps, participant/task metadata, and cost telemetry
paper_section: Not a current-paper RQ; current Section 10 and Section 12 identify approval load and real-pilot evaluation as future work
evidence_or_next_gate: Freeze pilot sites, task allocation, governance policy, productivity-loss threshold, telemetry, consent and privacy handling, and analysis plan before the pilot
